reasons: Starter data includes personal details and career claims that the owner must review.
Broken saved data is silently treated as no profile.

terms.meaning: a named shape for data, so the code knows which fields exist
written style rules given to the AI so its output sounds like the owner
a built-in example profile used to prefill the app
a small permanent storage space in a web browser, kept for one website

sections.name: ExperienceEntry
sections.title: Job entry shape
sections.what: Describes one job: company, role, dates, location, whether it is current, and a block of bullet points.
sections.why: Gives every job the same fields for the profile form and the AI prompts.
sections.watch_out: Bullets are stored as one text block separated by line breaks, not as a list.

sections.name: EducationEntry
sections.title: Education entry shape
sections.what: Describes one degree or school entry, with optional grade and achievements.
sections.why: Gives education records a consistent shape.
sections.watch_out: Optional fields may be empty, so code that prints them must check first.

sections.name: ProjectEntry
sections.title: Project entry shape
sections.what: Describes one project with a description, technology stack, outcome, and optional repository link.
sections.why: Used to show projects in the profile and to feed the prompts.
sections.watch_out: The outcome text is taken as given, and the prompts treat it as fact.

sections.name: Publication
sections.title: Publication entry shape
sections.what: Describes one publication with title, venue, year, and optional link.
sections.why: Gives publications a consistent shape for the profile and the research resume layout.
sections.watch_out: The year is stored as text, so sorting by year may behave oddly.

sections.name: Certification
sections.title: Certificate entry shape
sections.what: Describes one certificate with name, issuer, date, and optional note on relevance.
sections.watch_out: The date is text and may be empty, and the prompts print an empty date as blank.

sections.name: RoleType
sections.title: Career family names
sections.what: Lists the thirteen career families the app recognizes, such as engineering, sales, and research.
sections.why: Lets the resume layout and wording change by career family.
sections.watch_out: Renaming a family here breaks saved profiles that still use the old name.

sections.name: ROLE_TYPES
sections.title: Career family labels
sections.what: Pairs each career family with a display label and a short description for a picker on screen.
sections.why: Keeps the picker text in one place.
sections.watch_out: Each family in the names list needs a matching entry here, or it will be missing from the picker.

sections.name: Profile
sections.title: Full profile shape
sections.what: Describes the whole profile: contact details, headline, years of experience, lists of jobs, education, skills, projects, publications, certificates, voice notes, and timestamps.
sections.why: It is the single shape that every screen and prompt reads.
sections.watch_out: Contact fields are personal data and are sent to AI services through the prompts.

sections.name: getProfile
sections.title: Reading the saved profile
sections.what: Reads the saved profile from browser storage, or returns nothing if no profile exists or the data is broken.
sections.why: Uses the same safe read pattern as the other browser storage files.
sections.watch_out: Broken data becomes nothing without a message, so a corrupt profile looks like no profile at all.

sections.name: saveProfile
sections.title: Saving the profile
sections.what: Saves the profile with a new update time and announces the change so open screens refresh.
sections.why: Keeps the update time accurate and lets screens refresh without reloading.
sections.watch_out: It saves whatever it receives without checking the fields.

sections.name: hasProfile
sections.title: Checking for a saved profile
sections.what: Answers whether any profile is saved.
sections.why: Lets the app choose between first-time setup and the main screen.
sections.watch_out: It only checks that something is stored, not that the stored data is valid.

sections.name: getSeedProfile (part 1)
sections.title: Starter profile opening section
sections.what: Returns a built-in starter profile, starting with the owner's contact details, headline, and first job entries.
sections.why: Likely reason: a prefilled profile so the owner and new users do not start from a blank form.
sections.watch_out: The starter contains career claims that the AI prompts treat as verified, so each claim must be true before generating documents.

sections.name: getSeedProfile (part 2)
sections.title: Starter profile middle section
sections.what: Continues the starter profile with more job entries, the education record, and the skills groups.
sections.why: Same reason as the opening section: a complete example profile.
sections.watch_out: Job entries with empty bullets will produce prompts with no detail for that role.

sections.name: getSeedProfile (part 3)
sections.title: Starter projects section
sections.what: Adds the first group of project entries to the starter profile, each with a stack and an outcome line.
sections.why: Feeds the projects section of the profile and the notable builds part of the resume.
sections.watch_out: Outcome lines name employers and clients, so they must be accurate because the prompts use them as facts.

sections.name: getSeedProfile (part 4)
sections.title: Starter projects and publications
sections.what: Adds more project entries and the publication list to the starter profile.
sections.why: Same reason as the earlier sections: complete example data.
sections.watch_out: Some projects have no repository link, and the prompts simply leave that link out.

sections.name: getSeedProfile (part 5)
sections.title: Certificates and voice notes
sections.what: Adds the certificate list and the voice notes, which set the writing style and banned phrases for the AI.
sections.why: The voice notes tell the AI how to write in the owner's style, so the prompts depend on them.
sections.watch_out: Removing or editing the voice notes changes the tone of every generated document.

summary: Defines the shape of a career profile, saves it in browser storage, and includes a built-in starter profile.
purpose: Stores the user's career history, skills, and writing style, and supplies that data to the AI prompts.
why: Browser storage keeps the profile on the user's device. Likely reason for the built-in starter profile: a ready example to start from. The code does not say this.
how: 1) Define the shapes for jobs, education, projects, publications, certificates, and role families. 2) Save and read a single profile in browser storage. 3) Provide a built-in starter profile with contact details, job history, projects, publications, certificates, and voice notes.
inputs: Profile edits from the screens, and the built-in starter data.
outputs: A profile object, saved browser storage, and change events.
risks: The starter profile contains personal contact details and career claims that the AI prompts treat as verified facts. Saved data is not validated. Contact details are sent to AI services whenever prompts are built. The starter data ships in the app code, so anyone with the source can read it.
debug: If the profile looks empty, check the saved profile entry in browser storage and whether it parses. If generated documents contain wrong job facts, compare the saved profile and the starter data with the real record. If a screen does not update after a save, check that it listens for the profile change event.
